doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: The importance of rhythm guitar and playing without a stand
summary: Bucky says rhythm guitar is what dancers feel in a big band, and that he needs no music stand.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I don’t know I have to say I’ve been able to sit beside you a couple of times playing and it’s been a big thrill. And I just look at you chomping away there and there’s like nothing like that.
Yeah, that’s the whole ball game. I think that’s the most important thing in any big band was the rhythm guitar. That’s what the people danced to.
And sometimes you could hardly hear it.
I remember the last Fallcoming concert we did and we were playing Dick Hyman’s charts.
Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
And you had a really long piece. It was like five or six pages long. And I said, “Bucky do you want another stand?” And do you remember what you said?
You said basically, naaa, I don’t want a stand at all. Because you don’t need a stand.
